featured_videos.title: Day 72 Return to Pure Lion Diet Update
featured_videos.creator: Ferrigno Freedom
featured_videos.editorial_title: Day 72 Return to Pure Lion Diet Update
featured_videos.commentary: Dante's doing what a lot of people won't. he's being real about how quickly things fall apart when you deviate from what actually works for your body. The comment thread is full of people saying the same thing: dairy triggers anxiety, anything but pure meat brings back headaches, one slip and you're dealing with inflammation or brain fog all over again. What's striking is how visible the difference is. People aren't just saying they feel better on strict lion diet, they're literally seeing it in his energy and skin. That's the thing about elimination diets that people miss. when you strip everything away and find your baseline, you can't unsee how much certain foods were messing with you. Grief and stress are real factors here too, which connects to something we've talked about before with anxiety and diet, and it sounds like Dante's using carnivore as his anchor point while dealing with some heavy stuff.

featured_videos.title: I Read the Carnivore Diet Science So You Don't Have To
featured_videos.creator: Unnatural Vegan
featured_videos.editorial_title: I Read the Carnivore Diet Science So You Don't Have To
featured_videos.commentary: I appreciate the effort to dig into actual research instead of just arguing from ideology, but here's what I'm noticing in these comments: a lot of people are frustrated because the conversation keeps happening at the *study level* instead of the *experience level*. One commenter mentioned feeling better than ever after two weeks, while another's talking about lowering cholesterol through actual effort. those are real data points that matter. The truth is, we have limited long-term carnivore studies because the diet wasn't mainstream until recently, so personal experience and case reports aren't worthless, they're often all we've got. If you're curious about whether this works *for you*, the only real test is trying it and paying attention to how you feel, your energy, your bloodwork over time. That's not placebo, that's just biology being personal.

featured_videos.title: Pay Attention to What This 70-Year-Old Carnivore Did
featured_videos.creator: Shawn Baker MD
featured_videos.editorial_title: Pay Attention to What This 70-Year-Old Carnivore Did
featured_videos.commentary: The comment that keeps popping up is dead accurate: thousands of people are getting off meds and fixing their health on carnivore, and somehow that's still "anecdotal" while one study funded by Big Pharma gets called gospel. Eva at 70 doing what people half her age can't isn't luck or an outlier, it's what happens when you actually pay attention to how your body responds to food. The pushback in that interview wasn't about science, it was about protecting a system that profits from people staying sick and dependent. What's wild is the comments are full of 70, 75, 83-year-olds saying the same thing Eva is saying, building muscle, ditching meds, actually living instead of just existing, and the mainstream response is basically "yeah but what about the planet?" It's almost funny if it wasn't so frustrating.

featured_videos.title: This Carnivore Bowl Is All I Want to Eat
featured_videos.creator: Meet Carnivore
featured_videos.editorial_title: This Carnivore Bowl Is All I Want to Eat
featured_videos.commentary: What I love about this bowl is how honest it is. Ground beef, eggs, cheese, cream, sausage. No hidden ingredients, no complicated techniques, just real food stacked together. The comments show exactly why this resonates with people, too. Someone's making homemade cured meats and bone broth instead of buying processed versions. Another person's calling out the dairy sensitivity issue, which matters because not everyone tolerates it the same way. That's the thing about carnivore that videos like this make clear: the foundation works for most people, but the details are personal. You might nail this exact bowl, or you might swap the dairy for pure fat and get better results. Either way, you're working with whole foods you can actually see and pronounce.

featured_videos.title: The BEST Carnivore Ground Beef Recipes OF ALL TIME!
featured_videos.creator: HomeSteadHow
featured_videos.editorial_title: The BEST Carnivore Ground Beef Recipes OF ALL TIME!
featured_videos.commentary: Ground beef is the workhorse of carnivore cooking, and this video nails why. What stands out in the comments is people saving containers, using dehydrators, meal-prepping meatballs for the freezer, making beef chips. they're not just cooking, they're solving the real problem of "what do I actually eat this week" on a budget. That's the gap between theory and Tuesday night dinner. The air fryer crowd and cast iron purists both showed up too, which is the whole point: ground beef works in almost any kitchen setup, and it doesn't require a $300 gadget to shine. If you've hit a stall or bored yourself into a corner with the same three cuts, these recipes are exactly the kind of practical rotation that keeps people consistent. Protocol beats novelty every time.

featured_videos.title: They Are LYING To You About BEEF
featured_videos.creator: Dr. Tony Hampton - The Metabolic Health Doc
featured_videos.editorial_title: They Are LYING To You About BEEF
featured_videos.commentary: You can feel the frustration in that comment about styrofoam and plastic wrapping, and honestly, it's valid. Quality matters, but here's what I'm seeing from people in our community: most aren't waiting for perfect sourcing to feel dramatically better. That person turning 70 in November after switching to carnivore at 67? That's the real story. The beef conversation has gotten so tangled up in "is it a superfood or a poison" that we miss what actually matters for most people. which is that removing processed foods and focusing on nutrient density changes everything. Dr. Hampton nailed it on TMAO and the processed vs. minimally processed distinction. If you're curious about how beef fits into a sustainable carnivore approach, we've covered the quality and sourcing questions before, but the truth is, progress beats perfection every single time.
